title: B.A Semester I — Pre-Assessment (Diagnostic)
subject: Arts bridge (English, History, Political Science, Social Science)
scheme: Karnataka UG SEP 2024 / NEP 2020 — Sem I readiness
university: Bengaluru City University (template — substitute the college's affiliating university)
instructions: This is a diagnostic paper given in Week 1. It is not a university examination and does not count toward SEE.
It checks PUC / Class 12 Arts readiness for B.A Semester I (languages, History, Political Science, Economics/Sociology combinations).
Answer all questions. Figures to the right indicate marks.
Write the Section E answer in about 180–220 words.
sources: Karnataka 2nd PUC History, Political Science, Sociology, Economics and English
KSHEC NEP model syllabi for B.A History (Political History of Karnataka) and Political Science (Basic Concepts in Political Science)
Constitution of India — Preamble, Fundamental Rights, basic structure (PUC / AECC Constitution of India later in the degree)

sections.name: English language
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.text: The students asked, "When is the internal test?"
The students asked "When is the internal test."
The students asked, when is the internal test?
The students asked; When is the internal test?

questions.explanation: A direct question inside quotation marks keeps its question mark; a comma introduces the quote.

questions.text: "The minutes were approved by the committee." The voice of this sentence is:
questions.explanation: Be + past participle (were approved) with a by-agent is passive.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to "succinct".
questions.explanation: Succinct = expressed in few words without losing meaning.

questions.text: Identify the tense: "By next June she will have completed her internship."
questions.explanation: Will have + past participle = future perfect (action complete before a future point).

questions.text: A topic sentence in a paragraph usually:

options.text: States the main idea of that paragraph
Must be a quotation from a poem
Contains only examples and no claim

questions.explanation: The topic sentence carries the controlling idea; other sentences support it.

questions.text: Choose the correctly reported sentence. Direct: He said, "I am writing an essay now."

options.text: He said that he is writing an essay now.
He said that he was writing an essay then.
He said that I was writing an essay now.
He said that he wrote an essay tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Present continuous → past continuous; now → then; pronoun I → he.

questions.text: Which word is a synonym of "ancient" as used in "ancient inscriptions"?
questions.explanation: Ancient = belonging to a remote past; useful when reading History sources.

questions.text: In the sentence "Although it rained, the rally continued," the word Although introduces a:
questions.explanation: Although / though / even if mark concession — a dependent clause.

questions.text: Choose the option that is NOT a feature of a formal letter.
questions.explanation: Formal letters avoid slang and keep a polite, compact register.

questions.text: "The Western Ghats are older than the Himalayas." This sentence is:
questions.explanation: Older than = comparative. Superlative would be oldest.

sections.name: History & Political Science
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: Ashoka's dhamma is known mainly from:

options.text: His edicts inscribed on rocks and pillars

questions.explanation: Major and minor rock edicts and pillar edicts are the primary sources for Ashoka's dhamma.

questions.text: Hampi was the capital of which empire?
questions.unit: PUC History / B.A History of Karnataka
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara (Hampi) is a UNESCO site and a core B.A History of Karnataka topic.

questions.text: Kittur Rani Chennamma is remembered for:

options.text: Leading resistance against the British at Kittur (1824)

questions.explanation: She opposed the Doctrine of Lapse / British interference at Kittur — a standard Karnataka PUC example.

questions.text: The States Reorganisation Act that created a united Mysore (later Karnataka) linguistic state belongs to the year:
questions.explanation: 1 November 1956: linguistic reorganisation. The state was renamed Karnataka in 1973.

questions.text: The Harappan civilisation is also called:
questions.explanation: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are type-sites of the Indus (Harappan) civilisation.

questions.text: The Constitution of India came into force on:
questions.explanation: Adopted 26 Nov 1949 (Constitution Day); enforced 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day).

questions.text: Which of the following is a Fundamental Right?

options.text: Right to property (as it stands today, a legal right not a FR)
Fundamental Duty to vote in every election

questions.explanation: Right to property was removed from FRs by the 44th Amendment (now Art. 300A). Voting is a legal/constitutional right, not listed as a Fundamental Duty.

questions.text: India is described in the Preamble as a:
questions.explanation: Socialist and Secular were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

questions.text: In a parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
questions.explanation: Art. 75(3): the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People.

questions.text: Which feature best describes Indian federalism?

options.text: States may secede by a simple majority
A strong Centre with a division of powers in the Union, State and Concurrent lists
Governors are elected by state assemblies only

questions.explanation: India is a Union of States with three lists (Seventh Schedule) and a strong Centre; Governors are appointed by the President.

sections.name: Society & Economy
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: Urbanisation refers to:

options.text: An increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities
The caste system becoming more rigid

questions.explanation: Urbanisation is the process and the rising urban share of population.

questions.text: Which statement about caste in contemporary India is most accurate?

options.text: Caste has no legal or social existence today
Untouchability is abolished by the Constitution, but caste still shapes marriage, politics and inequality
Caste exists only in villages, never in cities

questions.explanation: Art. 17 abolishes untouchability; caste as a social structure persists in many domains.

questions.text: HDI (Human Development Index) combines:

options.text: Health, education and standard of living

questions.explanation: UNDP HDI: life expectancy, education (mean/expected years of schooling), GNI per capita.

questions.text: A poverty line is:

options.text: A cut-off of income/consumption used to count the poor

questions.explanation: Poverty lines (Tendulkar, Rangarajan, etc.) are thresholds; headcount ratio is the share below the line.

questions.text: Sex ratio in Indian census terms is usually expressed as:

options.text: Number of males per 100 females only
Literacy of women minus literacy of men

questions.explanation: Census of India: females per 1,000 males. Child sex ratio uses ages 0–6.

questions.text: Which is a Directive Principle of State Policy, not a Fundamental Right?

options.text: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases

questions.explanation: DPSPs (Part IV) are non-justiciable guidelines; FRs (Part III) are enforceable.

questions.text: The Green Revolution in India is associated with:

options.text: HYV seeds, irrigation, fertilisers and a rise in foodgrain output from the 1960s
The abolition of zamindari in 1950 only

questions.explanation: Wheat (and later rice) HYVs, especially in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

questions.text: Globalisation, in the Indian 1991-reform sense, mainly involved:

options.text: Closing the economy to all trade
Liberalisation, privatisation and greater integration with world trade and capital
Returning to a wholly planned licence-permit raj

questions.explanation: LPG (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) is the PUC shorthand for 1991 reforms.

questions.text: A social movement is best described as:

options.text: Collective, organised effort to promote or resist social change

questions.explanation: Examples: farmers' movements, environmental movements, women's movements, anti-caste struggles.

questions.text: Which river is central to a long-running inter-state water dispute involving Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Cauvery dispute (Karnataka–Tamil Nadu, also Kerala and Puducherry) is a staple of Karnataka civic awareness.

sections.name: Short answers
sections.instructions: Answer in 4–6 sentences. Each question carries 2 marks.

questions.text: State two differences between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.modelAnswer: FRs (Part III) are justiciable — courts can enforce them; DPSPs (Part IV) are non-justiciable guidelines for the State. FRs limit the State (civil-political rights); DPSPs ask the State to pursue socio-economic goals (welfare). In a conflict, FRs generally prevail, though later amendments and cases have sought harmony.

questions.text: Why are Ashokan edicts important as historical sources?
questions.modelAnswer: They are contemporary royal inscriptions in Prakrit (and other languages), spread across the subcontinent. They record Ashoka's dhamma, administration and after the Kalinga war, and can be compared with Buddhist texts and archaeology. As public documents they are less filtered than later chronicles.

questions.text: Explain any two causes of urbanisation in India after 1991.
questions.modelAnswer: Growth of services and industry in cities (IT, construction, informal work) pulls rural labour. Distress in agriculture and better perceived education/health in towns push migration. Liberalisation expanded private investment in metro regions (e.g. Bengaluru, Pune).

questions.text: Write two sentences in reported speech: (1) The teacher said, "Submit the assignment tomorrow." (2) She said, "I have visited Hampi."
questions.modelAnswer: (1) The teacher told us/them to submit the assignment the next day. (2) She said that she had visited Hampi.

questions.text: What is meant by 'unity in diversity' in the Indian context? Give one cultural and one political illustration.
questions.modelAnswer: It means many languages, religions and regions coexist within one political community. Cultural: multiple classical and folk traditions (e.g. Kannada, Tamil, Hindi literatures) under a shared civilisational space. Political: a single Constitution with federal states and official recognition of scheduled languages.

questions.text: "Local history is a way into national history." Taking any one example from Karnataka (Vijayanagara / Kittur / unification of the State / a freedom-movement episode), explain how a regional event helps us understand a wider Indian process. Mention at least one type of source a historian would use.
questions.unit: B.A History Sem I — Political History of Karnataka (bridge)
questions.modelAnswer: A strong answer (i) picks one case, (ii) narrates it briefly with dates, (iii) links it to a pan-Indian theme (state formation, colonialism, nationalism, linguistic federalism), (iv) names a source type (inscriptions, colonial records, newspapers, oral history, monuments), (v) closes with a caution about not treating the region as a mere illustration. Example: Vijayanagara as a Deccan state in the post-Sultanate world — Hampi monuments + Portuguese travelogues + inscriptions; or 1956 reorganisation as the working of linguistic federalism after the States Reorganisation Commission.
